topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the scope of the cancer lecture series, and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Risks, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of cancer etiology by evaluating how intrinsic mutational processes, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures interact to drive malignancy across populations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive malignant transformation, focusing on the cooperative mechanism between malaria and Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical Mutagens, Metabolism, and DNA Adducts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific dietary, environmental, and chemical agents undergo metabolic activation to induce direct DNA damage, adducts, and mutational transversions.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation and Promotion Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters and chronic inflammation drive the clonal proliferation of initiated cells through signaling pathways.

topics.label: Host Developmental Susceptibility and Principles of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how developmental timing and tissue context govern susceptibility to carcinogens, synthesizing the mechanistic principles of cancer development discussed so far.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the sequencing, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine and evaluate the carcinogenicity of environmental agents.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising key takeaways regarding environmental causes of cancer and contextualising exposure within everyday risk-benefit decisions.
